recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future change to whether history Bundles must carry response.status should be handled as a new conformance decision, not as a reapplication of FHIR-19619.
issue_request: FHIR-19619 was Published with a Persuasive resolution for the RESTful history interaction. It reported that _history prose implied Bundle.entry.response.status could be omitted even though the Bundle definition makes that element 1..1, and the approved resolution was to replace the optional-status sentence with successful-interactions and 200 OK guidance.
initial_application: The issue was applied by e8104dd10d, which changed source/http.html from the old sentence about not populating response.status to the approved wording. Current source still contains that replacement wording, and the obsolete optional-status sentence is absent.
additional_context: The current history section also says each history entry SHALL contain a response element, and later history examples include response.status values. The Bundle source still defines Bundle.entry.response.status as 1..1, so the contradiction was resolved by clarifying history guidance rather than changing Bundle cardinality. The Jira-linked Zulip thread supports this interpretation, and no relevant Confluence record was found. The related FHIR-23013 reconciliation is already represented on the combined branch and further confirms current history/status guidance is consistent.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The reconciliation published an empty audit commit on the combined branch documenting that current source satisfies FHIR-19619.

related_jiras.note: Later Published issue in the same history response-status area corrected examples and response.lastModified guidance; it is already represented on the combined branch by c6e0fc8266 and was used only as context.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive issue reported a conflict between _history prose that implied response.status could be omitted and Bundle.entry.response.status being 1..1.
evidence_items.learned: The approved decision was to clarify history guidance with successful-interactions and 200 OK wording, not to relax Bundle.entry.response.status.

evidence_items.summary: The current history section requires a response element, shows response.status in history examples, and contains the approved successful-interactions/200 OK note.
evidence_items.learned: The current RESTful API source already implements FHIR-19619 and no longer implies response.status may be omitted.

evidence_items.summary: Bundle.entry.response.status is still defined as a required 1..1 string with a short description of 'Status response code (text optional)'.
evidence_items.learned: The Bundle cardinality remains required, so the seed was resolved by fixing the history prose rather than changing the element definition.

evidence_items.summary: The Jira-tagged GF#19619 commit replaced the old optional-response.status sentence in source/http.html with the approved successful-interactions/200 OK wording.
evidence_items.learned: This confirms the issue was applied directly in source history.

evidence_items.summary: The Jira-linked thread identified the response.status contradiction and led to the change proposal; Lloyd McKenzie said cardinality could not change for R4 but expectations could be clarified.
evidence_items.learned: Community context supports the current clarification approach and does not suggest changing Bundle.entry.response.status.
